Question Choices: A rectangle has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. What is its area? (Just put the values, no units needed)
Hints: Use the perpendicular height in the area formula.
Solution: Rectangle area = base × perpendicular height = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

Hints: Use the perpendicular height in the area formula.
Solution: Parallelogram area = base × perpendicular height = 7 × 6 = 42 cm². The slanted side is not the perpendicular height.

Solution: h=A/b. Height A=60/12=5 cm; height B=60/6=10 cm. Check: 12×5=6×10=60.

Question Choices: Select. A parallelogram and a rectangle have the same base and height. Why do they have the same area? (A) Because both shapes have four sides (B) Because the slanted sides of a parallelogram are equal to the rectangle’s sides (C) Because you can cut and move part of the parallelogram to form a rectangle without changing the area (D) Because a parallelogram is always a rectangle: ~~A | B | C | D~~
Hints: Think about preserving all the pieces while making a rectangle.
Solution: Cut and translate pieces to make a rectangle with the same base and perpendicular height, with no gaps or overlap. Moving the pieces adds or removes no area. Four sides alone do not determine area; a parallelogram need not be a rectangle. Therefore C.
